title: The Auction
video_title: Tulip Mania: The Flower That Fooled History

segments.text: Haarlem, February 1637. According to a satire printed that year, an auctioneer kept lowering his price. Again, and again, and again.
Nobody bought a thing. At the height of the mania, one Semper Augustus bulb had sold for 10,000 guilders.
So how does a flower become a fortune, then nothing at all?

summary_for_next: Haarlem, February 1637: an auction finds no buyers, weeks after a Semper Augustus bulb sold for 10,000 guilders. Central question: how does a flower become a fortune, then nothing?
